card.line: Crete is a large island in the Mediterranean Sea where Paul's ship sailed along its coast on the way to Rome and where Paul later left Titus.

moments.title: Sailing along Crete
moments.text: Paul's ship sailed to the lee of Crete and stopped at Fair Havens. Paul warned that the trip was dangerous, but most chose to sail on toward Phoenix, a harbor in Crete, to spend the winter.

moments.title: The storm after leaving Crete
moments.text: A gentle south wind began to blow, so the ship sailed along the coast of Crete. Soon a cyclone called the Northeaster swept down across the island and drove the ship off course.

moments.title: Paul reminds the men
moments.text: After many days without food, Paul told the men they should have listened and not sailed from Crete. He urged them to take courage, because God had promised that no one's life would be lost.

moments.title: Titus left in Crete
moments.text: Paul wrote that he left Titus in Crete to set in order what was unfinished. Titus was to appoint elders in every town.
